root_cause.classification: test-side ordering assumption, not a product race
root_cause.summary: The test read module.runtime.store.read_freshness_snapshot()['receipts'][-1] as 'this pull's receipt'. Receipts are sorted by (finished_at, ingest_run_id); finished_at comes from connectors/base.py _utc_now() with microsecond=0 (1s precision) and ingest_run_id is a random uuid. When two consecutive pulls finish in the same second, receipts[-1] is arbitrary, so the 60-capped pull could be read as the previous 256-row pull ('assert 256 == 60'). Pulls are sub-second on a fast runner (10.9s failing run), hence 2/5 flakiness; param-independent.
root_cause.ruled_out: _DEFER_ACK ContextVar leakage and _METADATA_CACHE sharing: the debug trace showed total_failed=0, one receipt per pull, and the real 60-row pull receipt existing with normalized_count=60. Product pull semantics unchanged.
root_cause.deterministic_reproduction: Original test body with connectors.base._utc_now frozen to a constant fails 3/3 with 'assert 256 == 60' (receipt of previous pull selected).

fix.change: pull() snapshots receipt ids before the POST and returns the single new receipt. All assertions (256 x5, 60, delivered 1340/1377, quarantine) unchanged. Added regression param 'preclose-same-second-receipts' which freezes _utc_now so all receipts tie, reproducing the failure before the fix.
